summary: Develop practical digital fraud, cyber-enabled crime, and AML convergence skills for banking, mobile money, and insurance. Enquire today.
lede: Digital fraud and financial crime risk management connects fraud typologies, customer and channel risk, suspicious funds movement, and information-security safeguards across banking, mobile money, and insurance environments. The course shows you how to move beyond isolated fraud queues, AML monitoring, and cybersecurity responses by linking account takeover, device compromise, social engineering, SIM-swap activity, mule accounts, and merchant fraud to proportionate controls. You will build practical risk assessments, map fraud and AML events, design rule and alert-tuning matrices, analyse transaction and device indicators, and prepare investigation escalation packs. Using the FATF risk-based approach alongside ISO/IEC 27001:2022, NIST CSF 2.0, and related industry principles, you will learn to prioritise reliable alerts, connect fraud proceeds to suspicious activity, and document decisions for governance or reporting.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who investigate, prevent, govern, or report digital fraud and cyber-enabled financial crime across banking, mobile money, and insurance operations. It suits intermediate practitioners who already work with customers, transactions, alerts, incidents, or channel controls and need a stronger convergence model.
modules: Digital Fraud and AML Risk Foundations
prerequisites: You should have working exposure to banking, mobile money, insurance, fraud operations, AML controls, cybersecurity, transaction monitoring, or digital product governance. No programming is required. Basic spreadsheet skills help with the monitoring and KPI exercises, while advanced analytics and machine learning are treated at conceptual or operational application level rather than implementation level.
